deck: RENTING VRAM, NOT HASHING: 4090, 5090, 3090 AND CMP 170HX RIGS TESTED ON VAST, RUNPOD, SIMPLEPOD AND SALAD
MEMORY BANDWIDTH OVER TERAFLOPS: 8-GPU HGX BASEBOARDS, INFERENCE ENGINES, SIP TRUNKS AND A2P 10DLC SMS
site_ui.lead: Operators who moved from crypto mining to AI rentals report that the money now sits in renting VRAM, with Salad 4090s netting about $2.92 a day, a 10x CMP 170HX server pulling $36.37 in a day, and memory capacity and bandwidth, not headline teraflops, pricing data-center silicon.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, with every claim carrying timestamped inline attribution to its speaker and source video. Coverage runs from hand-built rental rigs, data-center GPUs and marketplace hosting through colocation, FinOps, neocloud brokerage, Kubernetes GPU sharing, inference engines and token routing to SIP trunking, A2P 10DLC and carrier compliance.

flow: Test any used GPU in person before paying, price-check it on gpudeals.net, and play OEMs against each other, as with Dell at $1M versus Supermicro at $750K.
Run the C-Payne stress tool for 48 hours to a week, watch for throttling such as a 4090 dropping from 450 W to 230 W, and reseat or swap risers one at a time if System interrupts climb.
Size PSUs, PDUs and rack circuits for a steady 80% load, put IPMI on its own out-of-band VLAN, keep InfiniBand off the management switch, and hold GPUs under 83 C.
Rent capacity on marketplaces that take about 25% on Vast, 20% on SimplePod, or 10% plus 40 cents on Salad, never power-limiting below 90% on Salad.
Benchmark tokens per GPU across more than one inference server, since Ollama showed an H200 at near-parity with an H100 at 36.6 tok/s, and price silicon on memory capacity and bandwidth.
Wire voice-AI telephony over SIP trunks and CPaaS carriers, then register and vet A2P 10DLC campaigns to deliver business SMS within carrier compliance.
